genxml.title: O2 CRIME memory transfer engine registers and tile layout
genxml.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
genxml.doc: CRIME memory transfer engine registers, address word and tile geometry.

struct.name: MODE
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Table 7-15 gives the register as 32 bits, readable and writable (established, [spec] PDF 183). Bits 31:12 are reserved (established, [spec] PDF 184). Bit 11 selects clear (0) or copy (1) (established, [spec] PDF 184). Bit 10 is described as enabling stipple application during clear operations; the table prints its values as 0 and 1 with enable and disable in that order. The X server sets bit 10 for its stippled fill (established, docs/mte.md), so 1 means enabled (inferred). Pixel depth value 3 is reserved (established, [spec] PDF 184). Buffer selector value 7 is reserved in both the source and destination fields (established, [spec] PDF 184 and 185). Bits 1 and 0 ask for ECC when reading the source and when writing the destination (established, [spec] PDF 185).

struct.name: BYTEMASK
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Table 7-15 gives the byte mask as 32 bits, readable and writable (established, [spec] PDF 183). Its bit polarity and bit-to-byte order are not stated in the specification (unknown).

struct.name: STIPPLEMASK
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Write-only, and marked non-global in Table 7-15 (established, [spec] PDF 183). Reads are not defined.

struct.name: FG
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The clear value, 32 bits, readable and writable (established, [spec] PDF 183).

struct.name: SRC0
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Source start address, framebuffer or linear, 32 bits, readable and writable (established, [spec] PDF 183).

struct.name: SRC1
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Second source address word, framebuffer or linear, 32 bits, readable and writable. Table 7-15 describes it as a start address, the same as src0 (established, [spec] PDF 183).

struct.doc: Destination start address, framebuffer or linear, 32 bits, write-only and marked non-global (established, [spec] PDF 183).

struct.doc: Null register, write-only and marked non-global (established, [spec] PDF 184). Its effect is not stated (see docs/mte.md).
